artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer r ≥ 1. An r-colored permutation of length n is a pair (σ, c) where σ ∈ S_n is a permutation and c : {1,...,n} → {1,2,...,r} is an arbitrary coloring. To each r-colored permutation one associates a Young diagram with at most r rows via a colored analogue of the Robinson–Schensted correspondence (the colors determine which of r interleaved insertion procedures the corresponding letter participates in, so that the resulting recording shape has at most r rows).

Equip the set of r-colored permutations of length n with the uniform probability measure, and let λ^{(n)} denote the random Young diagram (with at most r rows) obtained from a uniform random r-colored permutation of length n.

Problem. Develop a theory of limit shapes for Young diagrams with at most r rows analogous to the Vershik–Kerov–Logan–Shepp theorem for unrestricted Young diagrams under Plancherel measure. Concretely:

(a) Determine the asymptotic behavior, as n → ∞, of the row lengths λ_1^{(n)} ≥ λ_2^{(n)} ≥ ... ≥ λ_r^{(n)} of λ^{(n)}, including their typical growth rates.

(b) Identify a deterministic scaling (a_n, b_n) such that the rescaled boundary of λ^{(n)} (viewed as a Young diagram in the plane, with rows scaled by 1/a_n and columns by 1/b_n) converges, in an appropriate sense (e.g. in probability with respect to uniform or Hausdorff distance on the boundary curve), to a deterministic limit shape Φ_r supported on a region of the plane.

(c) Describe the limit shape Φ_r explicitly.

The case r = ∞ (no row restriction, with appropriate normalization corresponding to Plancherel measure on partitions of n) reduces to the classical Vershik–Kerov–Logan–Shepp limit shape; the goal is to produce the analogous theory for each finite r ≥ 1.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published theory of limit shapes for Young diagrams with at most r rows arising from uniform r-colored permutations. Classical limit-shape results (Vershik–Kerov, Logan–Shepp, and extensions to multiplicative/Plancherel-type measures) address unrestricted diagrams, and no source was found resolving the bounded-row, r-colored analogue. The problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Limit shapes of Young diagrams. Two elementary approaches
status_evidence.snippet: Techniques have been developed for obtaining the limit shapes of Young diagrams with respect to multiplicative measures, which arise in statistical mechanics.
status_evidence.claim: Existing limit-shape literature treats unrestricted Young diagrams under multiplicative/Plancherel measures rather than the r-row, r-colored permutation setting.

status_evidence.title: The limit shape of random permutations with polynomially growing cycle weights
status_evidence.snippet: Studies limit shape of Young diagrams associated to random permutations under particular classes of multiplicative measures.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on limit shapes from random permutations does not cover Young diagrams with at most r rows from r-colored permutations.
